method: BASELINE. Written straight from the deposited text with the writing-l4-rules skill (and references/regulative.md), from the seat of the individual to whom the law is applied, with the design defaults ruled on 2026-10-18 and the rulings on negatives of 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 (JUST FALSE where the text says no, NOTHING with a NOTHING-kind tag where it does not answer, case-by-case sites in the fork register); five regulative rules (s 40 making an application in time, s 62(2) requesting reasons, s 62(2) the Tribunal providing reasons, Sch 4 cl 8(2) renewing proceedings, s 84(2) and Sch 6 cl 14(2) instituting a court appeal) run by EVALTRACE inside exported questions that take only plain facts; no REFUSE; checked with the stable l4 of VS Code extension 1.6.98, JL4_LIBRARY_PATH unset. No pipeline, no coverage table, no independent test pass, no human gate.
edition_encoded: Civil and Administrative Tribunal Act 2013 No 2 (NSW), corpus document nsw_legislation:2024-07-01/act-2013-002 from the Open Australian Legal Corpus (collected 10 March 2025; unofficial, possibly out of date), as deposited at ../../registers/source-bundle/act-2013-002.txt (text sha256 523074c72b132978f646a01b4a4520d2969b76bc74259a8b9f75211c380c81ff per its meta.json)

seat: the party to proceedings in the NSW Civil and Administrative Tribunal: usually the applicant bringing a claim (tenant, consumer, home owner, retail lessee, discrimination complainant, person seeking review of a government decision such as victims support), and on appeal the appellant; a respondent asks the same questions; the victim in an offender's restitution review as witness (Sch 3 cl 13B)
focus: the provisions a claimant meets: jurisdiction (Part 3), federal matters (Part 3A), starting, conducting and deciding proceedings (Part 4 Divisions 2-5), enforcing and contravening orders (Part 5), appeals (Part 6), and the Division Schedules' representation, costs, renewal, court-relationship and appeal clauses

scope: In: ss 28-31, 34B, 34C(1)(a),(2), 40-41, 43, 45(1)-(3), 50, 53(3)-(4) as to s 50(3), 55, 59, 60, 61, 62(2),(2A), 71, 72, 76(2), 77(3),(5), 78, 32, 80, 82, 83, 84(2); Sch 3 cl 9(1), 12(1), 13, 13B, 15-18; Sch 4 cl 5, 7, 8, 10, 12; Sch 5 cl 27, 29(1),(2),(4),(6),(9); Sch 6 cl 6, 9, 11, 12, 14(1),(2),(5). Out: Parts 1-2 and 7 and Schedules 1, 2, 7 (machinery and transitional), the Division allocation lists (the Division is asked), enforcement and contempt begun by the Tribunal or an authorised official, the Tribunal's and courts' open procedural powers and orders on appeal, information disclosure orders, and officials' rights of appearance.
